PA MHAD App Privacy Policy

Last updated: September 2026 (v1.2). The same policy is shown in the app under Settings → Privacy Policy.

Data We Collect

This app collects only the information you enter into your Mental Health Advance Directive forms, including:

  • Personal information (name, address, phone, date of birth)
  • Agent and witness information
  • Treatment preferences and medication lists
  • Digital signatures
  • Additional instructions

We do not collect analytics, crash reports, device identifiers, or location data.

How Data Is Stored & Protected

Your directive data is NOT transmitted to the app developer or any third party for storage.

This is a web app: your data is held in an in-memory database in your browser tab. If you close the tab or the app crashes, your work is kept on this device for about 10 minutes so you can reopen and recover it — then it is wiped. Nothing is written to a server. Export or print your directive to keep a permanent copy.

AI Features & Third-Party Data Sharing

If you choose to use the optional AI features (AI Assistant chat or AI Suggest), text you submit is sent to the AI provider you select — Google Gemini by default, or Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, or xAI Grok if you choose one and add your own key — for processing.

On Google's Gemini free tier, Google may:
Other providers handle your data under their own API data policies — review the policy of whichever provider you use.

  • Use your input/output data to improve their products
  • Allow human reviewers to read your inputs and outputs
  • Retain data indefinitely (no automatic expiration)

The app strips common personally identifiable information (SSNs, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, addresses, names, and facility names) before sending your text to any provider, but this is a best-effort filter and cannot guarantee complete removal.

AI features are entirely optional. The app is fully functional without them.

Gemini Free Tier Data Practices

If you use the AI features with Google's free Gemini tier, be aware of the following:

1. Google retains AI conversation data indefinitely on the free tier. There is no automatic expiration.

2. Human reviewers at Google may read your inputs and outputs as part of their quality and safety processes.

3. Data sent to Gemini cannot be recalled or deleted by you or by this app. Once submitted, it is under Google's control.

4. If you are concerned about data privacy, consider upgrading to the paid Gemini tier, which offers stronger data protection policies and does not use your data for model training.

If you select a different provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, or xAI) instead of Gemini, that provider's own data and retention policy applies — review it before sending sensitive content.

You can avoid all third-party data sharing by not using the AI features.

International Users (GDPR)

If you are located in the European Economic Area (EEA), the UK, or Switzerland, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies to your use of this app.

Legal basis for processing: Your explicit consent, given through the in-app disclaimer and AI consent dialogs.

Your rights under GDPR:

  • Right to access: All your data is stored locally on your device — you have direct access at all times.
  • Right to erasure: Use "Delete All Data" in the app menu to permanently erase all local data.
  • Right to data portability: Export your directives as PDF or FHIR JSON (a standard health-records format) at any time.
  • Right to withdraw consent: Stop using AI features at any time; remove your API key to prevent further data transmission.
  • Right to restriction: You may use the app in Public Mode without any data persistence.

Data sent to your chosen AI provider is processed under that provider's own privacy policy and data processing terms. We cannot control or delete data once it has been sent.

US State Consumer Health Data Laws (CA, WA, CT, NV, NY)

This app may be subject to state consumer-health-data privacy laws including California (CCPA/CPRA), Washington (My Health My Data Act / MHMDA), Connecticut (CTDPA health provisions), Nevada (SB 370), and New York (Health Information Privacy Act).

Mental-health-directive content is "consumer health data" under each of these laws. Under all of them: (1) We collect mental-health treatment-preference data solely to help you create your advance directive. (2) We do not sell your health data — there is no commercial recipient. (3) The only third party that may receive any of your text is the AI provider you choose (Google Gemini by default, or Anthropic, OpenAI, or xAI), and only if you affirmatively opt in to AI features each session. (4) We use no third-party SDKs, no analytics, no advertising frameworks, no tracking pixels or cookies. (5) You may delete all locally stored data at any time via "Delete All Data" in the app menu.

Washington MHMDA includes a private right of action; we have designed the app to require explicit, per-session consent before any third-party transfer of consumer health data, and we treat written consent as conditional on the specific terms shown in the AI consent dialog.

For questions about your privacy rights, contact the developer using the channels listed in the Contact section below (multiple methods are provided per the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule).

Medical Reference Lookups (U.S. government data)

To help you fill in and understand your directive, the app looks things up in free, public U.S. government databases. These lookups use ONLY the single term or code needed for that lookup. They never receive your identity (your name, date of birth, address, or phone), the people you name (agents, witnesses, guardian), or your saved directive.

What is sent, and to whom:

  • Medication name you type → NLM RxTerms (autocomplete).
  • Condition name you type → NLM ICD-10-CM (diagnosis lookup).
  • A doctor / provider name you type into the optional doctor search → NLM NPI registry, used only to look that provider up in the public registry of healthcare providers.
  • A condition (by its ICD-10 code) or a medication (by name, resolved to a code via NLM RxNav) → NLM MedlinePlus Connect, to fetch a plain-language explanation.
  • A medication name → openFDA (U.S. Food & Drug Administration), to fetch that drug's official FDA label, which is used to ground the side-effects list.

No personal or identifying information is included in any of these requests — only the medical term, code, or provider name being looked up.

NLM, NIH, and the FDA are not responsible for this product and do not endorse or recommend it. These services are for information only and are not medical advice — consult a qualified professional. The NLM Clinical Table services are rate-limited to 20 requests/second.

Sources: U.S. National Library of Medicine (RxTerms, ICD-10-CM, NPI registry, RxNav, MedlinePlus Connect); U.S. Food & Drug Administration (openFDA).

PDF Export & Sharing

When you export a PDF of your directive, it is generated locally on your device. Sharing the PDF (via email, messaging, etc.) sends it through your device's standard sharing mechanism. The app cannot control where the PDF is stored once shared.

Your Rights

You can delete any directive at any time from the home screen. Deleting a directive removes all associated data (personal info, agents, medications, witnesses, signatures) from the local database.

You can remove your AI provider API key(s) at any time from the AI Setup screen.

Uninstalling the app removes all locally stored data.

No Third-Party Tracking

This app does not include any third-party analytics SDKs, advertising frameworks, crash reporting services (such as Firebase, Crashlytics, or Sentry), or tracking pixels.

The only external network connections this app makes are:

  • Your chosen AI provider — Google Gemini (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, or xAI — only when you use AI features
  • NIH/NLM Clinical Table Search Service — medication, condition, and provider (doctor) lookups
  • NLM MedlinePlus Connect & RxNav — plain-language condition and medication explanations (sends only an ICD-10 code or a medication name)
  • openFDA / U.S. FDA — official drug labels used to ground the side-effects list (sends only a medication name)

Each of these receives only the term or code being looked up — never your identity or your directive. No data is sent to the app developer at any time.

HIPAA & Compliance

This app is NOT HIPAA-compliant. It is not a covered entity or business associate under HIPAA. The app is intended for personal use by individuals preparing their own mental health advance directives.

While this app implements privacy measures aligned with GDPR, CCPA, and MHMDA principles (as described above), it has not been independently audited or certified for compliance with these regulations. If you require verified regulatory compliance, consult with a privacy professional before use.

Breach Notification

In accordance with the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule, if any unauthorized disclosure of your health information occurs through a security breach, we will notify affected users within 60 calendar days of discovering the breach.

Because this app stores data locally on your device and does not maintain a server-side database, breach risk is limited to the optional AI features. If your chosen AI provider notifies us of a breach affecting data sent through the app, we will pass that notification along through an in-app notice and a posting on the hosted privacy policy page.

Contact

The FTC Health Breach Notification Rule requires at least two contact methods. We provide:

  • In-app: an in-app breach notice will be shown the next time you open the app if a breach affects you.
  • Online: https://onica5000.github.io/MHAD/privacy.html (also used for breach postings if direct contact information is insufficient).
